cost: Hash insertion expected O(n) with hash assumptions, worst O(n²); paradigm merge linear scan can make O(records²). Storage O(input bytes+records+slots+blob). next_power_of_two, usize multiplication and u32 narrowing have no overflow certificate.
description: Compile-time dictionary encoder: lemma heap, open-addressed indexes, analyses/paradigms and generated word constants. Empty/unreadable input files become empty text; outputs are three sequential files.
forward: index(keys) allocates m=max(2,next_power_of_two(2n)), inserts i+1 at the first empty cyclic slot starting hash(key)&(m-1). main parses tag→lemma ID→count→source bits, builds analyses and UD-lowercase/AGID paradigms, then little-endian blob sections padded to four-byte boundaries. Word names first take punctuation, then first 5000 lowercase ASCII lemmas, then explicit constants; duplicate names retain the first assignment. Outputs lexicon.bin, lexicon_layout.rs, words.rs in that order.
inverse: R(slots)={ordered key lists K: index(K)=slots}; hash collisions and probing make R non-singleton. Blob plus layout recovers stored bytes and records within valid offsets, not skipped TSV columns, original source letter order or unknown source characters.
limitations: Only helper semantics and isolated synthetic build execution; no real dictionary quality validation
Output writes are not atomic, allocation/cast/overflow failures untested
No useful approximate semantics for binary compatibility
state: Input TSV bytes, lemma/form IDs, source bits, hash slots, byte offsets, OUT_DIR and filesystem.
